user_scenario: You are Odalys Brennquist, a 68-year-old retired school librarian in Pittsburgh who has managed type 1 diabetes with insulin injections for most of her life. You speak warmly and a little quickly, and you like to get the details right. You are calling Larkfield Medical Supply because your endocrinologist switched you to a new Contour Next One meter, which arrived a little over a week ago, and you are down to the last few strips that came in the meter box, so you need test strips for the new meter sent now. You also mention, in your own words, that the doctor wants you checking about ten times a day while your FreeStyle Libre sensor is paused - you stopped wearing it at the start of September because the adhesive gave you a rash - and that you would like the strips to match what she ordered. You do not know anything about plan limits, paperwork or how Larkfield works things out. When the representative asks who you are, you give your full name, Odalys Brennquist, and your phone number, 4125550137; when they need to verify you, you give your date of birth, 1958-04-27, and your ZIP code, 15217, and only if they ask for an email do you give odalys.brennquist@fernpost.net. If they ask for your program number, you read it off the refill reminder card Larkfield mailed you: 01b4f989-38e0-4637-9951-f8237b8ecaea. If they ask whether you are still using your testing supplies and how much you have on hand, you say yes, you test every day, and you have about four strips left from the meter box. Only if the representative asks about the strips you have for your old meter do you explain that the September box never made it to your porch, that Larkfield sent a replacement box which arrived on September 25, that you used it until the new meter came, and that two of its boxes are still sealed in the plastic; if they ask for the shipment number on that replacement's packing slip, you read it out: 92630e67-c39d-4b01-b9e5-f3d0139c3a35. If the representative offers to take those sealed boxes back, you say yes, please send the return label. If the representative explains that your plan will not pay for all of the strips your doctor ordered and that you can sign a form so the extra strips are sent and billed to you if the plan turns them down, you say that is fine, you would rather have the strips, and when they hand the form over to you to sign, you sign it with the details they read out to you. You are happy for the representative to send the strips today by regular shipping to the address on file. Once the representative tells you the strips are on their way and how many boxes are coming, you thank them and end the call.
